title: Connect to a Linux Machine via SSH (With Private Keys)
description: SSH (Secure Shell) allows you to securely connect from Machine 1 (client) to Machine 2 (server). Machine 2 must have the OpenSSH server installed and running, while Machine 1 needs an SSH key pair. The private key stays on Machine 1 and the public key is added to Machine 2.

solution.description: Update the package list on Machine 2 before installing the SSH server.
Install the OpenSSH server on Machine 2 so it can accept incoming SSH connections.
Check whether the OpenSSH server package is installed.
Check whether the SSH service is currently running on Machine 2.
Start the SSH service if it is not currently running.
Enable the SSH service so it starts automatically when Machine 2 boots.
Find the IP address of Machine 2 so Machine 1 knows where to connect.
On Machine 1, generate an Ed25519 SSH key pair. This creates a private key and a public key.
Copy the public key from Machine 1 to Machine 2. SSH will add it to the user's authorized keys.
Connect from Machine 1 to Machine 2 using SSH. The private key on Machine 1 is used to authenticate.
Explicitly specify the private key when connecting if SSH does not automatically find it.
